main_text.p: vel impetratorij [?] sunt, vel impetratorias antecedentes.

Et impetratoria [?] quidem causa posita est in una morte & resurrectioneChristi. Quod qua ratione factum sit ut mors Christi ista hominibus impetraret, ad rem quam agimus non attinet, & est ab AMYRALDO fusè explicatum Differ-tatione de Gratia universali. Ad rem nostram spectat quod effectus inæqualitas arguit proculdubio efficacitatis ali-quam inæqualitatem in causa.

Quando igitur vis illa Spiritus quae Gratia interna & subjectiva poteft appellari, per mortem Christi multis ho-minibus impetrata nulla est, consequens & consentaneum est ut Christus care-nus pro ijs mortuus non sit. Quod im-mane discrimen carenus inter eos & elec-tos constituit, atque adeo infinitam Gratiæ inæqualitate. Eo scilicet respecta Christus pro solis electis mortuus est.
Ad objectum quod attinet quandoquidem non aliunde manat communis illa gratia vocationis externæ quam ex aliqua efficacitate mortis Christi, necesse est ut carenus Christus pro omni-bus sit mortuus.

page.notes: Lines 1 and 2 of the first paragraph: the word "impetratorij" is hard to read, the final letter may be a long-s-like form. The word "Et impetratoria" has a mark through it that may be a printer's strike or a damaged letter. "resurrectioneChristi" is printed without a space. The page number may read 33 or 37. Reference marks in the margins (a star at the right of the line "quando-quidem", small marks near "Christus") are not transcribed as notes; no note text is printed. Doubtful: "poteft", "carenus" and "inæqualitate" are copied as printed; "carenus" may be a printing error for "catenus". The paragraph beginning "Quando igitur" starts with an indent and a decorated initial, so it is treated as a new paragraph.
